description: It gnaws boulders to keep its tusks short. When the grinding stops, something softer has wandered close.
lore: You find the stones a long time before you find the animal: boulders worn into a shallow saddle, glassy in the dip, three or four of them to a clearing. A teller once copied the grooves off one convinced they were writing, and got as far as ruling out four alphabets before somebody who had actually seen a brute took pity. They are teeth-marks. It grinds its tusks down on rock, all its life, on purpose.

Ask why an animal would file off its own best weapon and the answer is standing somewhere east, and has been standing there a very long time. A full-grown pair of tusks is a challenge, and there is only one thing in this country worth challenging, and [[monsters/gray_brute_2|the old bull]] has never lost. So they grind. Every young brute alive spends its whole span wearing itself smaller so it will not have to go and find out.

Almost everything else out in that country is at Habit by now, walking a round with the animal long since gone out of it. Not this one. It is entirely present — it is frightened, it is deciding, it grinds — and being present is precisely what the fear costs it. So watch the stones. When the wear on one goes grey and weathered and no fresh cut appears on it for a season, something has been settled out there, and it is a long walk east.
gm_notes: Come, and deliberately BRIGHT — the inversion of the usual monster note, since most wild things are stage three and this one's tragedy is that it is all there. Self-diminishment out of fear is the whole record. The abandoned grinding-stone is a hook a quest can hang off: the young one has grown them out and gone to Tuskmaul. Deliberately no NPC — this pair carries itself.
